jobs.title: Utility Technician I-IV
jobs.description_html:
General Description

Under general direction of the Distribution & Collection Superintendent or designee, an employee in this classification independently performs all functional duties in accordance with established procedures and standards to ensure efficient installation, maintenance, and repair of water mainlines, reuse lines, wastewater collection systems and their appurtenances for the City of Casselberry.


Hiring Salary is dependent upon experience and the position offered:

Utility Technician I: $43,381 - $54,227
Utility Technician II: $45,678 - $57,097
Utility Technician III: $47,310 - $59,138
Utility Technician IV: $49,029 - $61,286

Please see Typical Qualifications section below for the minimum requirements for each position.

Examples of Essential Functions

  1. Provides service and maintenance of water quality and sewer function. (90%)
    1. Assists in the installation and repairs potable and reclaim water mains and water service lines.
    2.  Assists in the installation of water service lines, water meters and meter boxes for customer water supply and water consumption monitoring.
    3. Independently installs and performs preventative maintenance services on water valves located on water main lines.
    4. Independently installs, repairs and performs preventative maintenance services on fire hydrants for firefighting department.
    5. Independently installs, repairs and performs preventative maintenance services on sewer force mains, gravity lines and sewer laterals.
    6. Responds timely to requests and work orders.
    7. Maintains tools, vehicles, and equipment assigned to employee by their supervisors.
    8. Participates in on-the-job training program and provides support to training staff.
    9. Performs all aspects of position in a manner consistent with departmental safety practices.
  2. Provides other distribution & collection related preventative maintenance activities (5%)
    1. Assists in the preventative maintenance of lift stations, verifies run times, inspects station and wet wells, and inspects generators and fluid levels on generators.
    2. Periodically assists the Utility Line Locator in accurately locating and marking underground city owned assets.
    3. Periodically assists the Inventory Control Specialist in the daily operations of the City’s inventory warehouse. 
    4. Periodically assist the Utility Heavy/Specialized Equipment Operator and utilize heavy equipment to excavate, load, or maintain City assets.
    5. Collects data for the utility asset management program.
  3. Additional Duties and Responsibilities (5%)
    1. Encourages and displays a daily teamwork driven mentality based on the unified divisional goals set forth by the Utilities Division Director or designee.  
    2. Performs all duties and responsibilities in a manner consistent with the core values of the City, and consistent with City and Department policies.
    3. Follows safe working practices and has a working knowledge of safety practices and procedures.
    4. Periodically performs after-hours/on-call rotation to respond to emergency repairs.
    5. Maintains facility and equipment for cleanliness and ongoing functionality.
    6. Replaces sod in assigned area.
    7. Restores asphalt and concrete in assigned area.
    8. Adheres to laws, regulations and policies of the City and of the assigned department.  Follows instructions provided by supervisor, Department Director or their designee.
    9. Completes the identified required or assigned training timely and applies acquired knowledge and/or skills.
    10. Participates in department meetings, staff meetings and other related activities. 
    11. Maintains, preserves, retains, and disposes public records pursuant to FS Chapter 119.
  4. Emergency Management Role 
    1. Participates as a member of the City staff as required to take action in the event of an emergency.
    2. Acts in the assigned role to support the City in disaster preparation and/or disaster recovery efforts as described in the City of Casselberry Emergency Management Plan, assigned by supervisor or designee.  As a member of the Public Works & Utilities Department may be responsible for the coordination of the maintenance and/or clearing of roadways, the operability of City’s fleet and prevention or drainage of local or area-wide flooding. In addition, as a member of the Public Works & Utilities Department may be responsible for the maintaining and/or rapidly restoring the operability of the City’s water and sewer systems.

(These essential and additional job functions are not to be construed as a complete statement of all duties performed.  Employees will be required to perform other job related marginal duties as assigned.)

Typical Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.  The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.  

  1. Education and Training:A High School Diploma or G.E.D. is required.  
  2. Experience:
    1. Utility Technician I: A minimum of one (1) year experience in water industry, sewer industry or related field is required. 
    2. Utility Technician II: A minimum of two (2) years experience in water industry, sewer industry or related field is required. A comparable combination of education and experience may be considered.
    3. Utility Technician III: A minimum of three (3) years experience in water industry, sewer industry or related field is required. A comparable combination of education and experience may be considered.
    4. Utility Technician IV: A minimum of four (4) years experience in water industry, sewer industry or related field is required. A comparable combination of education and experience may be considered.
  3. Certificates, Licenses and/or Registrations Required: All Utility Technicians must possess and maintain a valid Florida Class B (with tanker and air brakes endorsement) CDL Driver’s license. A Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) check will be made to determine acceptance of past driving record. In addition the below is required for each level:
    1. Utility Technician I: Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) Water Distribution System Operator Level III License.
    2. Utility Technician II: Must also possess Class C Wastewater System Operation Certification from a DEP approved entity, in addition to the above.
    3. Utility Technician III: Must maintain a Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) Water Distribution System Operator Level II License combined with Class C Wastewater System Operation Certification from a DEP approved entity or Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) Water Distribution System Operator Level III License combined with Class B Wastewater System Operation Certification from a DEP approved entity.
    4. Utility Technician IV: Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) Water Distribution System Operator Level II License. Class B Wastewater System Operation Certification from a DEP approved entity are required.
  4. Security Clearance: Florida Department of Law Enforcement background clearance.
  5. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
    • Knowledge (intermediate) of local, state and federal regulations affecting work.
    • Knowledge (intermediate level) of departmental rules, policies and procedures.
    • Knowledge of safety procedures for construction and repair of water and wastewater mains, reuse, and related construction projects.
    • Knowledge of the methods, materials, equipment, and techniques used in the installation, repair and maintenance of water, reuse and wastewater systems and related equipment.
    • Knowledge of the methods, practices, tools, materials and equipment of the pipe laying trades.
    • Knowledge (basic to intermediate level) of Central Square/NaviLine or similar utilities and work management software. 
    • Knowledge (basic) of Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) or similar software.
    • Knowledge (basic to intermediate level) of ArcMap or similar geographic information system software.
    • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with other employees and the public.
    • Ability to operate a motor vehicle and heavy equipment. 
    • Ability (basic to intermediate level) to utilize Microsoft Office Suite, e.g. Outlook, Work, and Excel.
    • Ability to support the mission statement of the City of Casselberry: Committed to protect and enhance the quality of life within its community.
    • Ability to support the core values of the City of Casselberry.
    • Ability to support the vision of the City of Casselberry: A vibrant, affordable, diverse, and progressive community where citizens feel safe, enjoy their neighborhoods, and access their city government.

Supplemental Information

The work environment and physical demands described here are representative and not intended to be all-inclusive of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job.   Reasonable accommodations may be made when requested to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

A.    Work Environment: This position performs the duties in a field setting.  The noise level in the work environment is loud.   This position is also frequently exposed to various weather conditions, working near moving mechanical parts, traffic hazards, fumes or airborne particles, noise extremes, slippery or uneven surfaces, and confined spaces. Occasionally, this position may be exposed to risk of electrical shock/explosives.

B.   Physical Demands: The primary functions require frequent periods of standing, walking, bending, pushing and pulling, driving, time sitting, using hands to handle or feel and reaching with hands and arms.  Occasionally this position will be required to climb or balance, jump, run or throw.  In addition, this position may be required to occasionally lift and carry up to one hundred (100) pounds with or without assistance of another person or utilization of lifting equipment.  This position is regularly required to use vision, speech and hearing, with or without assistive devices.

C.Equipment/Tools and Technology Used: This position utilizes the following tools and equipment while performing the duties of the job: Back hoe, track hoe, dump truck, city vehicle, Vac-Con, Smith Tapping Machine, pipes and applicable valves, hand tools (hammer, wrenches, screw drivers, etc.), power tools (compressor, jack hammer, chain saw, etc.), cell phone, computer and printer. 

D.   Employee Infection/Exposure Risk Classification:   Category II: Employee performs tasks that do not involve exposure to blood, body fluids or other potentially infectious materials (OPIM), however, employment may require performing unplanned Category I tasks.  The normal work routine involves no exposure to blood, body fluids or OPIM, but potential exposures may be required as a condition of employment.

jobs.title: Utility Heavy Equipment Operator
jobs.description_html:
General Description

The Utility Heavy Equipment Operator is responsible for operation of heavy and medium gasoline and diesel powered equipment to be utilized for the construction and repair of sanitary sewer lines, force water mainlines, high-pressure water mainlines, reuse lines, and sewer manhole excavations for the City of Casselberry.  The Utility Heavy Equipment Operator performs work independently within established policies and procedures.

Examples of Essential Functions

  1. Provides operation of heavy equipment for construction and maintenance of water quality and sewer function. (95%)
    1. Oversees or independently performs the operation of heavy/medium equipment, such gasoline and diesel powered equipment to excavate holes for installation and repair of gravity sewer, reuse lines, and water mains.
    2. Routinely oversees or independently operates advanced sewer cleaning trucks and equipment. 
    3. Ensures accuracy in excavation around other utility lines and ducts to avoid disruption in other types of services and required repairs.
    4. Oversees and independently ensures organization and maintenance of the Utility’s material storage, transfer, and disposal sites. 
    5.  Oversees and independently ensures proper maintenance and cleanliness of the Utility’s heavy and medium sized equipment.  
    6. Provides technical support of excavation and safety practices to pipe line installation crew.
    7. Assists in the installation, repairs and preventative maintenance services on sewer force mains, gravity lines and sewer laterals.
    8. Responds timely to requests and work orders.
    9. Maintains tools, vehicles, and equipment assigned to employee by their supervisors.
    10. Performs sod, asphalt, and concrete restoration as required.
    11. Assists in the installation/repair of water/reclaimed service lines, water/reclaimed meters and meter boxes.
    12. Performs all aspects of position in a manner consistent with departmental safety practices.
  1. Additional Duties and Responsibilities (5%)
    1. Encourages and displays a daily teamwork driven mentality based on the unified divisional goals set forth by the Utilities Director or designee.  
    2. Performs all duties and responsibilities in a manner consistent with the core values of the City, and consistent with City and Department policies.
    3. Follows safe working practices and has a working knowledge of safety practices and procedures.
    4. Performs after-hours/on-call rotation to respond to emergency repairs.
    5. Adheres to laws, regulations and policies of the City and of the assigned department.  Follows instructions provided by supervisor, Department Director or their designee.
    6. Maintains facility and equipment for cleanliness and ongoing functionality.
    7. Completes the identified required or assigned training timely and applies acquired knowledge and/or skills.
    8. Participates in department meetings, staff meetings and other related activities.
    9. Provide cross divisional training opportunities to other City employees when requested by Utilities Maintenance Manager or designee
    10. Maintains accurate daily logs of hours worked and work performed.
    11. Maintains, preserves, retains, and disposes public records pursuant to FS Chapter 119.
  1. Emergency Management Role 
    1.  Participates as a member of the City staff as required to take action in the event of an emergency.
    2.  Acts in the assigned role to support the City in disaster preparation and/or disaster recovery efforts as described in the City of Casselberry Emergency Management Plan, assigned by supervisor or designee.  As a member of the Public Works & Utilities Department may be responsible for the coordination of the maintenance and/or clearing of roadways, the operability of City’s fleet and prevention or drainage of local or area-wide flooding. In addition, as a member of the Public Works & Utilities Department may be responsible for the maintaining and/or rapidly restoring the operability of the City’s water and sewer systems.

(These essential and additional job functions are not to be construed as a complete statement of all duties performed.  Employees will be required to perform other job related marginal duties as assigned.)

Typical Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.  The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.  

  1. Education and Training: A High School Diploma or G.E.D. is required.
  2. Experience: A minimum of three (3) years’ experience in operation of large and medium size gasoline and diesel powered equipment or related field is required.   A comparable combination of education and experience may be considered.
  3. Certificates, Licenses and/or Registrations Required:  Must possess and maintain a valid Florida Class B (with tanker and air brakes endorsement) CDL Driver’s license (or ability obtain within 6 months), and a Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) Level  III Water Distribution System Operator License (or ability obtain within 15 months), and a Class  C Certification in Wastewater System Operation from a DEP approved entity (or ability obtain within 27 months) are required. A Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) check will be made to determine acceptance of past driving record.  
  4. Security Clearance: Florida Department of Law Enforcement background clearance.
  5. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
    • Knowledge (intermediate to advanced) of local, state and federal regulations affecting work.
    • Knowledge (intermediate to advanced) of departmental rules, policies and procedures.
    • Knowledge (intermediate to advanced) of safety procedures for construction and repair of water and wastewater mains, reuse, and related construction projects.
    • Knowledge (intermediate to advanced) of the methods, materials, equipment, and techniques used in the installation, repair and maintenance of water, reuse and wastewater systems and related equipment.
    • Knowledge (intermediate to advanced) of the methods, practices, tools, materials and equipment of the pipe laying trades.
    • Ability to utilize utilities and work management software. 
    • Knowledge (intermediate to advanced) of ArcMap or similar geographic information system software.
    • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with other employees and the public.
    • Ability to operate a motor vehicle and heavy equipment. 
    • Ability to utilize Microsoft Office Suite, e.g. Outlook, Work, and Excel.
    • Ability to support the mission statement of the City of Casselberry: Committed to protect and enhance the quality of life within its community.
    • Ability to support the core values of the City of Casselberry.
    • Ability to support the vision of the City of Casselberry:  A vibrant, affordable, diverse, and progressive community where citizens feel safe, enjoy their neighborhoods, and access their city government.

Supplemental Information

The work environment and physical demands described here are representative and not intended to be all-inclusive of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job.   Reasonable accommodations may be made when requested to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
A. Work Environment: This position performs the duties in a field setting.  The noise level in the work environment is loud.  This position is also frequently exposed to various weather conditions, working near moving mechanical parts, traffic hazards, fumes or airborne particles, noise extremes, slippery or uneven surfaces, and confined spaces. Occasionally, this position may be exposed to risk of electrical shock/explosives.
B. Physical Demands: The primary functions require frequent periods of standing, walking, bending, pushing and pulling, driving, time sitting, using hands to handle or feel and reaching with hands and arms.  Occasionally this position will be required to climb or balance, jump, run or throw.  In addition, this position may be required to occasionally lift and carry up to one hundred ( 100) pounds with or without assistance of another person or utilization of lifting equipment.  This position is regularly required to use vision, speech and hearing, with or without assistive devices.
C. Equipment/Tools and Technology Used: This position utilizes the following tools and equipment while performing the duties of the job: Back hoe, track hoe, dump truck, city vehicle, Vac-Con, , Smith Tapping Machine, pipes and applicable valves, hand tools (hammer, wrenches, screw drivers, etc.), power tools (compressor, jack hammer, chain saw, etc.), cell phone, computer and printer.
D. Employee Infection/Exposure Risk Classification:   Category II: Employee performs tasks that do not involve exposure to blood, body fluids or other potentially infectious materials (OPIM), however, employment may require performing unplanned Category I tasks.  The normal work routine involves no exposure to blood, body fluids or OPIM, but potential exposures may be required as a condition of employment.

jobs.title: Utility Maintenance Worker
jobs.description_html:
General Description

The Utility Maintenance Worker is responsible for participating in the installation, maintenance, and repair of water mainlines, refuse lines, lift stations, wastewater collection systems and other work in connection with the water and wastewater collection system operations for the City of Casselberry.  The Utility Maintenance Worker performs routine work well covered by existing policies, procedures or instructions and supervision is readily available.

Examples of Essential Functions

Provides service and maintenance of water quality and sewer function. (80%)

  1. Installs and repairs potable and reclaim water mains and water service lines.
  2. Performs installation of water service lines, water meters and meter boxes for customer water supply and water consumption monitoring.
  3. Participates in the preventative maintenance services on water valves located on water main lines.
  4. Participates in the install, repair and preventative maintenance services on fire hydrants for firefighting department.
  5. Participates in the install, repair and preventative maintenance services on sewer force mains, gravity lines and sewer laterals. 
  6. Responds timely to requests and work orders.
 
Provides preventative maintenance and repair to the lift stations. (15%)
  1. Participates in the preventative maintenance of lift stations, verifies run times, inspects station and wet wells, and inspects generators and fluid levels on generators.
  2. Performs preventative maintenance on pumps, valves (i.e. gate, check, and plug), electrodes, and solenoids.
  3. Participates in the maintenance of control units, control panels and devices; removes, replaces and reprograms pump control units (PCU), telemetry control units (TCU), and control panels.
  4. Verifies and tests voltage and amp transmitting to and from lift station.

 Additional Duties and Responsibilities (5%)
  1. Performs all duties and responsibilities in a manner consistent with the core values of the City, and consistent with City and Department policies.
  2. Follows safe working practices and has a working knowledge of safety practices and procedures.
  3. Performs after-hours/on-call rotation to respond to emergency repairs.
  4. Maintains facility and equipment for cleanliness and ongoing functionality.
  5. Replaces sod in assigned area.
  6. Restores asphalt and concrete in assigned area.
  7. Adheres to laws, regulations and policies of the City and of the assigned department.  Follows instructions provided by supervisor, Department Director or their designee.
  8. Completes the identified required or assigned training timely and applies acquired knowledge and/or skills.
  9. Participates in department meetings, staff meetings and other related activities.
  10. Maintains, preserves, retains, and disposes public records pursuant to FS Chapter 119.
 
Emergency Management Role 
  1. Participates as a member of the City staff as required to take action in the event of an emergency.
  2. Acts in the assigned role to support the City in disaster preparation and/or disaster recovery efforts as described in the City of Casselberry Emergency Management Plan, assigned by supervisor or designee.  As a member of the Public Works Department may be responsible for the coordination of the maintenance and/or clearing of roadways, the operability of City’s fleet and prevention or drainage of local or area-wide flooding. In addition, as a member of the Public Works Department may be responsible for the maintaining and/or rapidly restoring the operability of the City’s water and sewer systems.
 
(These essential and additional job functions are not to be construed as a complete statement of all duties performed.  Employees will be required to perform other job related marginal duties as assigned.)

Typical Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.  The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.  

  1. Education and Training:  A High School Diploma or G.E.D. preferred.  
  2. Experience:  A minimum of up to one (1) year experience in water industry, sewer industry or related field is required.   A comparable combination of education and experience may be considered.
  3. Certificates, Licenses and/or Registrations Required:  Must possess and maintain a valid Florida Class B (with tanker and air brakes endorsement) CDL Driver’s license which may be obtained within the first six (6) months of employment.  A Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) check will be made to determine acceptance of past driving record.
  4. Security Clearance: Florida Department of Law Enforcement background clearance.
  5. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
  • Knowledge of local, state and federal regulations affecting work.
  • Knowledge of departmental rules, policies and procedures.
  • Knowledge of safety procedures for construction and repair of water and wastewater mains, reuse, and related construction projects.
  • Knowledge of the methods, materials, equipment, and techniques used in the installation, repair and maintenance of water, reuse and wastewater systems and related equipment.
  • Knowledge of the methods, practices, tools, materials and equipment of the pipe laying trades.
  • Knowledge of Central Square/NaviLine or similar utilities and work management software. 
  • Knowledge of Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) or similar software.
  • Knowledge of ArcMap or similar geographic information system software.
  • Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing.
  • Ability to understand and follow written and oral instructions.
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with other employees and the public.
  • Ability to operate a motor vehicle and heavy equipment. 
  • Ability to utilize Microsoft Office Suite, e.g. Outlook, Work, and Excel.
  • Ability to support the mission statement of the City of Casselberry: Committed to protect and enhance the quality of life within its community.
  • Ability to support the core values of the City of Casselberry.
  • Ability to support the vision of the City of Casselberry: A vibrant, affordable, diverse, and progressive community where citizens feel safe, enjoy their neighborhoods, and access their city government.

  2.  The work environment and physical demands described here are representative and not intended to be all-inclusive of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Occasionally, this position may be exposed to risk of electrical shock/explosives.

jobs.title: Police Officer
jobs.description_html:
General Description

Under general direction, to perform police duties, such as; foot patrol, motorized patrol within the City of Casselberry; to prevent crime; to detect and arrest the perpetrators of crimes; to regulate traffic; to provide public assistance; to perform all additional functions for the rank as prescribed by relevant laws, city ordinances, departmental rules and regulations, orders and directives of the Police Department; to perform special duties and/or assignments as directed by the Chief of Police in his discretion; to enforce the laws of the State of Florida and the ordinances of the City of Casselberry.

IMPORTANT !! - YOU MUST READ THE SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION TO DETERMINE YOUR APPLICATION ELIGIBILITY:  

Examples of Essential Functions

- Patrols assigned zone in a police vehicle.
- Responds to emergency and non-emergency calls for police assistance as directed within the City of Casselberry.
- Arrests violators of state laws and city ordinances, as required.
- Directs and regulates traffic within the City.
- Investigates traffic accidents.
- Maintains the public peace.
- Provides general assistance to the public such as: to injured and ill persons, and in public and domestic disturbances.
- Inspects and protects business and residential properties in the nighttime.
- Completes and submits detailed written reports on approved forms on all activities.
- Appears in courts of law to present testimony and evidence in arrest cases.
- Follows safe working practices and has a working knowledge of safety practices and
procedures.
- In the event of a hurricane, major storm, natural or man-made disaster, which may threaten the area, the employee will be expected to work.  

Typical Qualifications


  • Be at least 19 years of age for law enforcement and correctional probation.
  • Be at least 18 years of age for corrections.
  • Be a citizen of the United States.
  • Have earned a high school graduate or equivalent (GED).
  • Have not been convicted of any felony or of any misdemeanor involving perjury or a false statement.
  • Any person who, after July 1, 1981, pleads guilty or nolo contendere to, or is found guilty of any felony or of a misdemeanor involving perjury or a false statement, shall not be eligible for employment or appointment as an officer, not-withstanding suspension of sentence or withholding of adjudication.
  • Have never received a dishonorable discharge from any of the Armed Forces of the United State.
  • Have good moral character.
  • Have successfully completed the Florida Basic Recruit Training Program for the respective discipline or completed the Equivalency of Training process. 
  • Have achieved a passing score on the State Officer Certification Examination.
  • Have been fingerprinted by the employing agency with prints processed by the FDLE and the FBI.
  • Have successfully passed a background investigation, to include drug testing.
  • Have passed a physical examination by a licensed physician, physician assistant, or certified advanced registered nurse practitioner.
 
  • - Qualify in a physical fitness test.
  • - Qualify in an oral review board.
  • - Qualify in a CVSA interview/examination.
  • - Qualify in a physical examination and medical testing administered by the City of Casselberry approved agent prior to employment.
  • - Qualify in a drug screen test.
  • - Qualify in a psychological fitness test administered by the City of Casselberry approved agent prior to employment.

Supplemental Information

APPLICATION ELIGIBILITY:
THIS IS NOT A SPONSORED/PAID POLICE ACADEMY POSITION. In order to be considered for this position, the applicant must have successfully complete a Florida Law Enforcement Officer Academy, be CURRENTLY attending a Florida Law Enforcement Officer Academy or CURRENTLY attending a Florida Cross-Over Law Enforcement Academy and is in good standing or has had their out-of-state Law Enforcement certification transferred over to a Florida Law Enforcement certification.

APPLICATION PROCESS:
- Applicants MUST complete the On-line Application and the Supplement Questions. If you do not have access to a computer with Internet, there is one available at your local library.
- The Recruitment Section will review your On-line Application and the Supplemental Questions. If you do not meet the minimum standards, you will be notified. If you do meet the minimum standards, you will be notified and an Application Packet will be E-mailed to you.
- The Application Packet must be completed either in Adobe and printed or printed and typed. Handwritten documents WILL NOT be accepted. The Application Packet must be complete with all required documents attached, signed, notarized (where applicable) and returned to the Casselberry Police Department by the designated date.
- The Recruitment Section will review your Application Packet. If you do not meet the minimum standards, you will be notified. If you do meet the minimum standards, you will be notified and invited to participate in the oral board interview, submit a writing sample, and take the Physical Abilities Test.
- The oral board interview and writing sample will be conducted in the Casselberry Police Department multi-purpose room at a predetermined date. Applicants that successfully pass the oral board interview and writing sample will be permitted to complete the PAT (Physical Abilities Test).
- The PAT will follow the oral board interview and writing sample. The PAT will be at Secret Lake Park (Maps and directions will be provided). Applicants will be notified immediately of their test time. (The parameters of the PAT are available from the Casselberry Police Department)
- The Recruitment  Section will compile all applicants' files and select the applicants that are going to be sent for a background review, held for further consideration or removed from the process. All applicants will be notified of their status.
- The background process will be handled by the Support Services Corporal and the Casselberry Investigations Section. This process will include, but is not limited to a voice stress examination; a fingerprint comparison; a neighborhood check and a review of the history concerning your employment, driving, credit, criminal history and drug usage. Dates and times associated with this process is at the discretion of the background investigators.  Applicants with acceptable backgrounds will advance to the Chief's Interview.
- The Chief's Interview will be conducted at the discretion of the Chief of Police. The Chief's Administrative Services Coordinator will contact the applicant to schedule the interview. The Chief of Police will select applicants that are going to be recommended for Conditional Employment Offers, held for further consideration or removed from the process. All applicants will be notified of their status by E-mail or phone call.
- Applicants that are given a Conditional Employment Offer will be advanced to the final step.
- The final step consists of a medical physical, drug screen and physiological review of the applicant. Applicants that fail any part of this step will be removed from  employment consideration. Applicants that pass all parts of this step will be authorized for a full-time position with the Casselberry Police Department. The Support Services Sergeant will coordinate the starting date with the new officer and the City of Casselberry Human Resources department.

APPLICATIONS MUST BE SUBMITTED ONLINE AT: http://www.casselberry.org

jobs.title: Intern - Creative Services
jobs.description_html:
General Description

We are seeking a Creative Services Intern to support our Creative Services team. This role offers hands-on experience working on a wide range of internal and external creative projects, while contributing original design, photography and video content. The ideal candidate is eager to learn, adaptable and excited to work across multiple creative disciplines.

Essential Functions

  • Support internal creative requests across departments
  • Assist with external-facing creative projects as needed
  • Create original graphic content for print and digital use
  • Assist with photography and video capture, editing and basic production
  • Help maintain brand consistency
  • Managing multiple projects while meeting deadlines

Minimum Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing a degree in Emerging Media, Digital Media, Multimedia or a related field
  • Junior or Senior
  • Proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite
  • Basic experience with photography and video production
  • Strong attention to detail and fundamentals
  • Ability to take direction and apply feedback
  • Please note:  Academic or professional portfolio may be requested during interview process

Physical Demands

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:  The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to handle or feel and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to reach with hands and arms. The employee is occasionally required to stand; walk and bend, kneel, squat, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus

WORKING CONDITIONS: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Environmental factors include indoor, flat surface, noise, sitting with occasionally walking and standing.

jobs.title: Accounting Supervisor or Accounting Manager - Capital & Fixed Assets
jobs.description_html:
General Description

The purpose of this position is to manage the accounting activities related to capital projects, construction work in progress (CWIP), and fixed assets in conformance with GAAP and Toho policy. This position reports to the Comptroller and is responsible for overseeing the full lifecycle of capital asset accounting, including project tracking, capitalization, reconciliation, and reporting. Key responsibilities include supervising accounting staff responsible for capital and fixed asset processes; ensuring accurate and timely capitalization of assets; maintaining detailed and auditable records; coordinating with Engineering, Procurement, Accounts Payable, and external consultants and vendors; and supporting financial reporting and audit requirements. This position will lead process improvements, strengthen internal controls, and ensure consistency and accuracy in capital accounting practices. The Accounting Supervisor/Manager will also provide analytical insight into capital spending and asset management to support organizational decision-making.

This individual will demonstrate strong leadership, technical accounting expertise, and the ability to manage complex workflows in a fast-paced environment.

Essential Functions


ACCOUNTING SUPERVISOR/MANAGER - ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

The purpose of this position is to manage the accounting activities related to capital projects, construction work in progress (CWIP), and fixed assets in conformance with GAAP and Toho policy. Key responsibilities include supervising accounting staff responsible for capital and fixed asset processes; ensuring accurate and timely capitalization of assets; maintaining detailed and auditable records; coordinating with Engineering, Procurement, Accounts Payable, and external consultants and vendors; and supporting financial reporting and audit requirements. This position will lead process improvements, strengthen internal controls, and ensure consistency and accuracy in capital accounting practices. The Accounting Supervisor/Manager will also provide analytical insight into capital spending and asset management to support organizational decision-making.

This individual will demonstrate strong leadership, technical accounting expertise, and the ability to manage complex workflows in a fast-paced environment.

Minimum Qualifications

ACCOUNTING SUPERVISOR - MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  1. Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business or related field.
  2. Minimum of five years relevant experience.
  3. Lead experience preferred.
  4. Equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered.
  5. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.

ACCOUNTING MANAGER - MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  1. Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business or related field.

jobs.title: Utility Worker (Biosolids)
jobs.description_html:
General Description

Under close supervision, the purpose of this position is to perform entry-level work in support of the Biosolids / Grounds Maintenance department of Toho Water Authority's water resources systems. Workflow involves performing semi-skilled manual labor, operating some heavy equipment, repairing irrigation lines, operating zero-turn mowers. Reports to the Field Services Foreman.


Essential Functions

Essential Functions:
  1. Must be physically able to operate a vehicle, load landscape trailers safely, and operate various hands-on power tools. Tasks involve the ability to exert heavy physical effort in the heavy work, typically involving some combination of climbing and balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching and crawling, lifting, carrying, pushing or pulling of objects and materials of moderately heavy weight (20-50 pounds) and occasionally very heavy weight (in excess of 100 pounds).
  2. Performing skills from basic irrigation repair to safely operating a chainsaw, pole saw, drills, and other power tools. Mowing grass with different types of mowers and small tractors.
  3. Running errands, identifying and purchasing parts and tools in assistance to our team mechanic.
  4. The ability to adapt to the needs of the public when asked to do various tasks at a moment's notice which involve garbage removal, tree trimming, etc. 

Minimum Qualifications

Any combination of training and experience that would provide the required knowledge, skills and abilities is qualifying.  A typical way to obtain that required qualification would be:

Education & Experience

  • A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
  • This is an entry-level position; previous relevant work experience is preferred but not required.
  • Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License. Class B is preferred.
KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES:
  • Strong writing, editing, and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor messages for diverse audiences.
  • Experience leading communications in crisis or high-pressure situations.
  • Familiarity with construction, infrastructure, or utility industry communications a plus.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Proficiency in communications tools, including media monitoring, social media management, and content creation platforms.

Physical Demands

PHYSICAL DEMAND:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand and walk to a significant degree; use hands to operate tools or feel and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to pull, push, kneel, bend, squat, crawl, and twist. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 75 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

jobs.title: Plant Mechanic (Preventative Maintenance) - II, Senior, or Master
jobs.description_html:
General Description

Plant Mechanic II: $25.10 - $33.41 Hourly
Senior Plant Mechanic: $26.82 - $35.74 Hourly
Master Plant Mechanic: $32.13 - $45.90 Hourly


The purpose of this position is to support Water and/or Wastewater Plant operations by performing preventive and reactive maintenance and repairs to systems and equipment for assigned plant(s).  Duties may include troubleshooting and repairing or replacing a variety of pumps, motors, valves, etc.  

Essential Functions

Plant Mechanic II: 

  1. Ability to effectively communicate and coordinate with vendors, pump representatives, and contractors on-site to request quotes and discuss project requirements.
  2. Demonstrate ability to conduct comprehensive condition assessments of system components to identify issues and determine maintenance or repair needs.
  3. Competence in interpreting technical drawings, blueprints, and schematics to understand equipment configurations and assembly or disassembly procedures.
  4. Demonstrate ability to conduct insulation resistance tests using a Megger instrument to assess the insulation condition of electrical components.
  5. Demonstrate proper utilization and interpretation of thermal imaging camera outputs to identify potential issues or anomalies within the system.
  6. Demonstrate ability to inspect and replace wear rings on submersible pumps to ensure optimal performance and longevity.
  7. Demonstrate working knowledge of hydraulic and pneumatic systems commonly used in industrial machinery, including the ability to troubleshoot performance issues, identify component failures, and perform routine maintenance.
  8. Demonstrate ability to safely remove and install impellers on submersible pumps as part of maintenance or repair procedures.
  9. Demonstrate the ability to evaluate pump performance by analyzing key parameters such as flow rate, pressure, total dynamic head (TDH). Power consumption, and vibration levels.
  10. Proficiency in working with electrical systems, including wiring, circuitry, and control panels.
  11. Skilled in replacing bearings and performing precise alignment of motors and pumps to minimize vibration, reduce mechanical stress, and extend equipment lifespan.
  12. Demonstrate knowledge of P-Card and procurement procedures for acquiring necessary equipment and supplies.
  13. Skill in maintaining accurate records, logs, and documentation related to maintenance activities, repairs, and inspections.

Senior Plant Mechanic: 

  1. Understand the principles and processes involved in water and wastewater treatment, including filtration, sedimentation, disinfection, and chemical treatment.
  2. Familiarity with Toho Water standards and specifications, ensuring all equipment meets criteria.
  3. Ability to identify the need for and to submit GIS red lines for system updates.
  4. Ability to analyze data from monitoring equipment and make adjustments to optimize plant performance and efficiency.
  5. Demonstrate proficiency in welding and fabrication techniques to repair or members are informed and compliant with safety regulations.
  6. Proficiency in using computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS) and other software tools for scheduling maintenance, managing inventory, and documenting work activities.
  7. Demonstrate expertise in performing precision shaft alignment to ensure accurate alignment between motors, pumps, gearboxes, and other machinery components to reduce vibration, prevent premature wear, and extend equipment life in accordance with manufacturer specifications and industry standards.
  8. Identify need for confined space entry. Demonstrate understanding of procedures and oversee a team in performing confined space entry, ensuring adherence to safety protocols and regulations.
  9. Demonstrate an understanding of plumbing principles and the ability to work with pipes, fitting, and fixtures to ensure proper installation and functionality.
  10. Demonstrate proficiency in completing pre-hurricane preparation (72 hours prior) and level III hurricane response (36 hours prior) checklists, including placement of generators/bypass pumps for optimal response.
  11. Ability to effectively communicate with team members, supervisors and other stakeholders to coordinate tasks, report findings, and collaborate on projects.
  12. Identify training needs, develop and deliver a training presentation to the department.
  13. Demonstrate skill in handling escalated situations with customers/contractors effectively, maintaining professionalism and resolving issues promptly.

Master Plant Mechanic: 

  1. Demonstrate ability to effectively lead and coordinate a crew, delegating tasks and ensuring efficient workflow.
  2. Demonstrate proficiency in assigning work orders and generating preventative maintenance tasks within INFOR or CityWorks system.
  3. Demonstrate understanding or incident reporting protocols and procedures. Ability to accurately complete supervisor incident reports.
  4. Demonstrate understanding of payroll processes and procedures within ADP. Ability to effectively validate timesheets for payroll purposes.
  5. Proficient in interpreting and comprehending construction and engineering drawings. Demonstrate ability to accurately interpret plan designs for maintenance and repair tasks.
  6. Familiarity with equipment procurement processes and capital budgeting principles.
  7. Demonstrate knowledge of standby protocols and procedures and ability to effectively manage standby operations.
  8. Experience in implementing preventative maintenance programs to ensure optimal performance and longevity of equipment. Proficiency in planning and scheduling maintenance activities.
  9. Demonstrate an understanding of performance management policies and procedures. Participate in employee performance review process to evaluate employee performance. Provide assistance with processes related to documentation of employee conduct.
  10. Understanding of relevant regulations and guidelines governing treatment operations, including environmental standards and reporting requirements.
  11. Ability to evaluate entire system’s performance and understand how mechanical components interact with electrical and control systems.
  12. Demonstrated competency in time management and resources allocation for repair projects.
  13. Commitment to staying updated on advancements in water treatment technology, industry best practices, and relevant certifications or training opportunities.

Minimum Qualifications

Plant Mechanic II:

  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
  2. Minimum of five years relevant work experience working in either a utility or Industrial setting with a focus on motors, pumps, piping and control. 
  3. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
  4. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.
  5. As a condition of employment, must obtain State of Florida Class A Driver's License within first six months of employment.

Senior Plant Mechanic: 

  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
  2. Minimum of eight years’ relevant work experience working in either a utility or Industrial setting with a focus on motors, pumps, piping and control. 
  3. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
  4. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.
  5. As a condition of employment, must obtain State of Florida Class A Driver's License within first six months of employment.

Master Plant Mechanic: 

  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
  2. Minimum of ten years’ relevant work experience working in either a utility or Industrial setting with a focus on motors, pumps, piping and control. 
  3. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
  4. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.
  5. As a condition of employment, must obtain State of Florida Class A Driver's License within first six months of employment.

Physical Demands

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: 
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand and walk to a significant degree; use hands to operate tools or feel, and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to pull, push, kneel, bend, squat, crawl, and twist. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 75 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

WORKING CONDITIONS:
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Environmental factors include outdoor conditions; rugged terrain, slippery surfaces, varying weather, including, heat, cold, dry, wet weather. In addition, noise, darkness, brightness, vibrations, traffic, biological agents, chemicals, gas/ fumes, magnetic fields, or congested area. Environmental factors include indoor, flat surface, noise, sitting with occasionally walking and standing.

jobs.title: Senior Foreman of Field Services (Biosolids Department)
jobs.description_html:
General Description

The purpose of this position is to supervise the daily operations of the Biosolids Department and manage the safe, efficient transportation, disposal, and contract administration of biosolids and related hauling operations throughout the utility. This position is responsible for leading a team of Equipment Operators/Truck Drivers, managing multiple service contracts, overseeing departmental budgets, coordinating biosolids hauling for nine wastewater treatment facilities, and ensuring regulatory compliance.

This position serves as the primary liaison between Toho and multiple contracted service providers, develops long-term capital improvement plans and annual operating budgets, coordinates hauling schedules, oversees contractor performance, and provides leadership for departmental staff through training, performance evaluations, scheduling, and employee development. The employee also assists with procurement activities, contract development, capital planning, and continuous improvement initiatives that enhance operational efficiency and reduce operating costs.

Essential Functions

Senior Foreman of Field Services (Biosolids Department)

1. Manages Contracts and Vendors – Administers contracts such as grounds maintenance, weed control, biosolids hauling, and other service contracts. Monitors contractor performance, reviews invoices, resolves issues, assists with negotiations, and supports the development of bid documents.

2. Supervises Staff – Directs and manages Equipment Operators/Truck Drivers by assigning work, coordinating schedules, approving timecards and leave, conducting performance evaluations, providing training and coaching, and administering corrective action as needed.

3. Manages Biosolids Hauling Operations – Oversees biosolids hauling for nine water reclamation facilities, ensuring regulatory compliance, efficient transportation, and uninterrupted disposal operations.

4. Manages Disposal Sites – Oversees sand and grit disposal sites supporting lift station maintenance, ensuring proper operations, environmental compliance, and cost-effective disposal practices.

5. Manages Budgets – Develops and administers the annual Capital and Operating Budgets for the Biosolids Department and monitors expenditures.

6. Manages Fleet and Equipment – Coordinates vehicle and heavy equipment utilization, scheduling, preventive maintenance, and replacement planning.

7. Ensures Regulatory and Safety Compliance – Ensures operations comply with applicable safety regulations, environmental requirements, permits, and departmental procedures.

8. Improves Operations and Controls Costs – Identifies and implements opportunities to improve efficiency, optimize equipment and contractor utilization, reduce costs, and enhance service delivery.

9. Coordinates Internal and External Activities – Serves as a primary point of contact between Toho staff, contractors, regulatory agencies, and utility management to coordinate work and resolve operational issues.

10. Performs Administrative and Procurement Functions – Prepares purchase requests, reviews invoices, maintains records, prepares reports, supports procurement activities, and assists with departmental planning.

11. Performs Other Duties – Performs other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate's ability to successfully perform the essential functions of the position will be considered.

· Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in utility operations, heavy equipment operations, transportation, biosolids management, contract administration, or related field.

· High School Diploma or GED issued from an approved administrator.

- Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.

· Minimum of two (2) years of supervisory experience that includes assigning work, coordinating schedules, approving timecards and leave, conducting performance evaluations, providing training and coaching, and administering corrective action as needed.

Desired Qualifications

· Experience supervising transportation, hauling, or biosolids operations.

· Experience managing contractor performance and administering service contracts.

· Experience developing operating and capital improvement budgets.

· Knowledge of biosolids transportation, disposal regulations, and environmental compliance.

· Possess and maintain a valid Florida Class A Commercial Driver License (CDL).

· Experience with procurement processes and contract development.

· Knowledge of heavy equipment operations and fleet management.

· Strong leadership, organizational, budgeting, and communication skills.

· Ability to analyze operational data and identify cost-saving opportunities.

· Ability to effectively resolve contractor and operational issues while maintaining positive working relationships.

· Working knowledge of computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS), GIS, Microsoft Office, and financial management software.

Physical Demands

Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand and walk to a significant degree; use hands to operate tools or feel, and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to pull, push, kneel, bend, squat, crawl, and twist. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

Working Conditions

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Environmental factors include outdoor conditions; rugged terrain, slippery surfaces, varying weather, including, heat, cold, dry, wet weather. In addition, noise, darkness, brightness, vibrations, traffic, biological agents, chemicals, gas/ fumes, magnetic fields, or congested area.

Environmental factors include indoor, flat surface, noise, sitting with occasionally walking and standing.

Emergency Response

This job title is classified, for Emergency Preparation and Response Policy, as Essential

Time and Attendance Classification

Time and Attendance Classification: Flexible Work Schedule

Remote Work Classification

This position is eligible for remote work consideration

jobs.title: Business Process Specialist - All Levels
jobs.description_html:
General Description

Business Process Specialist I: $26.82 - $35.74 Hourly
Business Process Specialist II: $28.69 - $38.25 Hourly
Senior Business Process Specialist: $32.13 - $45.90 Hourly

The Business Process Specialist is responsible for analyzing, documenting, modeling, and improving business processes across the organization to enhance operational efficiency, service quality, and organizational effectiveness. This role works closely with the Business Transformation Manager to facilitate process discovery workshops, develop process models using BPMN standards, identify improvement opportunities, and support the implementation of process changes.

The Business Process Specialist will work closely with the business stakeholders to document and improve processes across the entire enterprise. He/ she will serve as a bridge between business units and technology teams, ensuring that business requirements, process documentation, and improvement initiatives are effectively aligned with organizational objectives. While the primary focus of the role is process management and continuous improvement, the position also supports technology-related initiatives by collaborating with IT teams, reviewing system impacts, and helping translate business needs into functional requirements as and when necessary.

The ideal candidate is passionate about understanding how work gets done and helping teams improve it. They are comfortable leading process modeling workshops, documenting workflows using BPMN standards, applying Lean Six Sigma techniques, and partnering with both business and technology teams to deliver sustainable process improvements. They can effectively facilitate conversations, challenge assumptions, and translate ideas into actionable process improvements.

Essential Functions

Business Process Management

  • Facilitate process discovery, process mapping, and process improvement workshops with stakeholders across the organization.
  • Document current-state and future-state business processes using BPMN (Business Process Model and Notation) standards.
  • Maintain and govern process documentation repositories to ensure consistency, accuracy, and accessibility.
  • Analyze workflows, procedures, and business operations to identify inefficiencies, bottlenecks, risks, and improvement opportunities.
  • Develop process maps, swim lane diagrams, value stream maps, and supporting documentation.
  • Assist business units in defining process performance measures and key performance indicators (KPIs).
  • Support the development and maintenance of process governance standards, methodologies, and best practices.

Continuous Improvement

  • Apply Lean, Six Sigma, and other continuous improvement methodologies to improve business performance.
  • Conduct root cause analyses and facilitate problem-solving sessions.
  • Recommend process improvements that reduce waste, improve customer experience, enhance compliance, and increase operational effectiveness.
  • Support implementation and change management activities associated with process improvement initiatives.
  • Monitor and measure the effectiveness of implemented process changes.

Business and Technology Collaboration

  • Collaborate with business and IT stakeholders to understand process and system dependencies.
  • Analyze how applications and technology solutions support business processes and identify alignment opportunities.
  • Participate in software implementation, workflow automation, and digital transformation initiatives as needed.
  • Support user acceptance testing (UAT), process validation, and solution adoption activities.

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Build collaborative relationships with leaders, subject matter experts, and frontline employees.
  • Facilitate workshops, interviews, and cross-functional working sessions to elicit process knowledge and improvement opportunities.
  • Present findings, recommendations, and process models to stakeholders at various organizational levels.
  • Provide guidance and coaching on process management methodologies and standards (if needed)

Minimum Qualifications

  1. Bachelor’s degree in relevant field
  2. 1-3 years process mapping/analysis
  3. Awareness of flowcharts and swimlane diagrams
  4. Awareness of basic Lean and Six Sigma concepts
  5. Facilitate SME interviews to document process models

jobs.title: Business Support Manager
jobs.description_html:
General Description

Review of applications will begin on September 28, 2026.  The position will remain open until a candidate is selected.

Salary: $83,845- $119,787

The Business Support Manager provides leadership and coordination across departmental training, quality assurance, workforce management, and business support functions for the Customer Service Department. This role ensures alignment with departmental goals, service standards, data integrity requirements, and continuous improvement initiatives while promoting operational effectiveness and service excellence.

Essential Functions

  • Provide day-to-day leadership, coaching, and performance management for staff supporting departmental training, quality assurance, workforce management, and business support functions.

  • Maintain a working knowledge of core responsibilities across assigned functions, including curriculum development, onboarding, scorecard management, quality reviews, survey tracking, forecasting, scheduling, data audits, user acceptance testing (UAT), technology support, and process documentation.

  • Ensure departmental training materials, procedures, and standard operating documentation are accurate, current, and consistently applied across the Customer Service Department.

  • Lead quality assurance programs, including scorecard development, quality standards, coaching trends, compliance monitoring, and identification of opportunities to enhance the customer experience.

  • Support workforce management initiatives that optimize staff resources by evaluating call volumes, staffing needs, schedules, schedule adherence, and resource allocation to meet service-level goals.

  • Oversee business systems support by identifying system issues, validating data integrity, coordinating user acceptance testing, and facilitating communication between business operations and Information Technology.

  • Analyze operational trends, performance metrics, audit results, and other data to identify opportunities and recommend improvements to training, processes, systems, staffing, and service delivery.

  • Collaborate with other Customer Service leaders to address operational gaps, improve consistency, strengthen cross-functional coordination, and enable teams to focus on day-to-day service excellence.

  • Communicate priorities, risks, project status, performance trends, and opportunities for improvement to the Director of Customer Service.

Minimum Qualifications

Any combination of education and experience that demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.

· Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Management, Communications, Information Systems, or a related field.

· Seven years of progressively responsible experience in customer service operations, business support, training, quality assurance, workforce management, business analysis, or a related operational support area, including at least three years of experience in a supervisory, lead, project management, or team coordination role that included providing guidance, setting priorities, coaching employees, or leading cross-functional initiatives.

· Demonstrated ability to analyze and interpret operational reports, quality results, staffing data, customer feedback, audit findings, and performance metrics to identify trends, recommend corrective actions, and support continuous improvement.

· Experience developing, reviewing, or maintaining procedures, training materials, scorecards, dashboards, workflows, or process documentation.

· Working knowledge of customer service technology, case management systems, reporting tools, call center platforms, billing systems, or other business applications used to support service delivery.

· Experience coordinating cross-functional work with operations, IT, training, quality, workforce management, or leadership teams.

· Strong leadership, communication, organization, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

· Experience in a utility, municipal, government, call center, or high-volume customer service environment.

· Experience supporting system implementations, user acceptance testing, data audits, reporting improvements, or process automation initiatives.

· Experience leading or supporting employee development, onboarding, quality monitoring, performance coaching, or customer experience improvement programs.

· Familiarity with workforce forecasting, scheduling, adherence monitoring, service level tracking, or resource planning.

· Strong ability to translate operational needs into clear business requirements, training needs, process changes, and measurable improvement plans.

jobs.description_html:
General Description

Salary:
Trainee: $20.46 - $25.57 Hourly ($24,557 - $53,186
Operator I (C License): $23.41 - $31.23 Hourly ($48,693.00- $64,958.00 Annually)
Operator II (B License): $25.07 - $33.41 Hourly ($52,146.00 - $69,493.00 Annually)
Operator III (A License): $26.82 - $35.74 Hourly ($55,786.00 - $74,339.00 Annually)

The purpose of this position is to operate and maintain the water treatment plant and the drinking water for the public. This is accomplished by collecting daily meter readings; calibrating lab meters; checking plant equipment; adjusting the SCADA computer; checking charts for trends; performing oil changes and greasing; repairing equipment; collecting daily plant samples; recording dissolved oxygen readings; inspecting chlorine cylinders; communicating problems; creating and fulfilling work orders; completing plant and system checks; verifying equipment operation; evaluating trends; and verifying chemical residuals. Other duties include performing UV maintenance and repair; training employees; troubleshooting for plant malfunctions; creating monthly operation reports; managing monthly water charts and plumage reports; developing a majority of the forms the Water Plants use; replying to e-mails; performing janitorial work; overseeing fire flow tests; and supervising contractors.

Essential Functions

Trainee:

  1. Performs daily water plant checks by checking all equipment; monitoring hour meters and flow meters; checking chemical residuals; changing chemical analyzers; maintaining chemical inventory; transferring and inspecting chemicals; calibrating test kits; and adjusting feed rates.
  2. Performs all housekeeping duties by hosing down areas with debris; addressing safety concerns; checking for proper drainage; painting; disposing of trash; assisting with landscaping or beautification projects; and ensuring the facility is maintained.
  3. Collects samples for analysis by using gloves and caution in sampling areas; managing sampling containers carefully; avoiding contaminations; fulfilling chain of custody forms; and obtaining all information for chain of custody forms.
Operator I (C License):
  1. Performs daily water plant checks by checking all equipment; monitoring hour meters and flow meters; checking chemical residuals; changing chemical analyzers; maintaining chemical inventory; transferring and inspecting chemicals; calibrating test kits; and adjusting feed rates.
  2. Maintains the plant by completing maintenance work orders; greasing plant equipment; managing rust/corrosion control; and performing housekeeping practices and general cleaning.
  3. Manages plant repairs by scheduling work orders for internal repair; ensuring all plant equipment in repaired; and assisting mechanics and electricians when necessary.
Operator II (B License):
  1. Performs preventive maintenance by shutting off power; locking out equipment; greasing moving equipment; changing oils in gear boxes; guaranteeing all maintenance activities are safe; and painting equipment. 
  2. Controls processes by checking process basins; using odor sensory perception and results from laboratory tests; reviewing the performance of the process; and overseeing the SCADA system. 
  3. Performs housekeeping duties by cleaning for spider webs; removing all dirt and debris; maintaining materials and equipment; and ensuring the facility is aesthetically pleasing. 
  4. Gives plant tours by evaluating the process and equipment in the treatment process; obtaining daily readings from meters and gauges; maintaining records; and ensuring all equipment functions properly. 
  5. Maintains facility log books by recording duties and projects; maintaining a record of compliance issues; and maintaining entries of process issues and the integrity of the log book. 
  6. Obtains samples for analysis by using gloves and caution when approaching sampling areas; handling sampling containers carefully; closing sample containers promptly; filling out chain of custody forms; and collecting information for chain of custody form.
  7. All other duties as assigned.
Operator III (A License):
  1. Fulfills water plant daily operations by visiting individual facilities; collecting plant data; collecting samples to analyze residuals in water leaving the facility; making any necessary adjustments to chemical feed pumps; recording in log book all the details; and checking remote wells for normal operations. 
  2. Completes monthly work orders by pulling up assigned work orders; reviewing and prioritizing work orders; designating which are to being completed; and completing tasks on work order. 
  3. Remains updated with chemical purchases by approving all chemical purchases for the finance department; copying and filing chemical purchase invoices; submitting purchase orders; and tracking all chemical purchases. 
  4. Manages and replies all company e-mails by opening e-mail account; filtering through information; saving important data; and replying to emails.
  5. All other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

Trainee:

  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
  2. This is an entry level position, previous relevant work experience is preferred but not required.
  3. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.

Operator I (C License):
  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
  2. Minimum of one-year relevant experience.
  3. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.
  4. State of Florida Drinking Water Treatment Plant Operator C License.

Operator II (B License):
  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator. 
  2. Minimum of three years relevant experience. 
  3. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
  4. State of Florida Drinking Water Treatment Plant Operator B License. 
  5. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.

Operator III (A License):
  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator. 
  2. Minimum of three years relevant experience. 
  3. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
  4. State of Florida Drinking Water Treatment Plant Operator A License.
  5. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.

Physical Demands

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand and walk to a significant degree; use hands to operate tools or feel, and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to pull, push, kneel, bend, squat, crawl, and twist. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

WORKING CONDITIONS:
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Environmental factors include outdoor conditions; rugged terrain, slippery surfaces, varying weather, including, heat, cold, dry, wet weather. In addition, noise, darkness, brightness, vibrations, traffic, biological agents, chemicals, gas/ fumes, magnetic fields, or congested area. Environmental factors include indoor, flat surface, noise, sitting with occasionally walking and standing.

Environmental factors include indoor, flat surface, noise, sitting with occasionally walking and standing.
